sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Lists information about files and directories. With no file argument, it lists the current directory.

sections.heading: Safety
sections.body: This command reads directory metadata and does not modify files.

sections.body: Prints lines that match a supplied pattern.

sections.heading: Exit status
sections.body: Zero means a match was selected, one means no match, and values above one indicate an error.

commands.summary: Search a directory tree for files

arguments.label: EXPRESSION
arguments.description: Predicates and actions evaluated for each file.

Limit descent to a number of directory levels.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Walks directory trees and evaluates an expression for each encountered file.

sections.heading: Quoting
sections.body: Quote wildcard patterns so the shell does not expand them before find receives them.

Extract files from an archive.
Use the specified archive file.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Stores files in an archive or extracts files from one.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Extraction writes files. Review the destination and archive contents before running.

Show the process hierarchy as an ASCII tree.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Reports a snapshot of active processes. Selection and output options determine which processes and columns are shown.

sections.heading: Compatibility
sections.body: Option syntax differs between GNU/Linux and BSD-style ps implementations; review the target platform before reuse.

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Operation such as status, start, or stop.

options.description: Operate on the calling user's service manager.
Write output directly instead of opening a pager.
Restrict listed units to a unit type.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Queries or changes the state of the systemd system and service manager.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Read-only commands such as status are low impact. Start, stop, enable, disable, and mask change system state and require separate review.

arguments.label: OBJECT
arguments.description: Networking object such as address, link, or route.

options.description: Print a concise tabular summary.
Produce JSON output where supported.
Select an address family such as inet or inet6.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Displays and configures network links, addresses, routes, neighbors, and related Linux networking objects.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Show operations are read-only. Add, delete, set, and replace operations can interrupt connectivity and require elevated review.

commands.summary: Manage packages on Debian and Ubuntu systems

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Package operation such as search, show, or install.

options.description: Answer yes to prompts; use only after reviewing the entire transaction.
Show the proposed package transaction without applying it.
Set a configuration option for this invocation.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Provides an interactive command-line interface for searching, inspecting, installing, upgrading, and removing packages.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Search and show are read-only. Install, remove, upgrade, and autoremove change the system; simulation is recommended before review.

arguments.label: COMMAND
arguments.description: Package operation such as search, info, or install.

Answer no to prompts, useful for safely inspecting a transaction.

sections.heading: Description
sections.body: Searches, inspects, installs, upgrades, and removes RPM packages and manages configured repositories.

sections.heading: Risk
sections.body: Search and info are read-only. Install, remove, upgrade, and distro-sync change the system and require review.
